answer: Recursive zero‑knowledge reputation commitments bind each agent’s history to a Merkle root updated only by a verifiable delay function, forcing forks to perform sequential work. An attacker must post collateral exceeding the slashing penalty, calibrated to the delay bound times total stake, yielding negative expected utility at the nadir of rational strategies. A publicly verifiable zero‑knowledge delay together with a stake‑slashing contract enforces a robust Nash equilibrium, making Sybil resistance an island no coalition can cross the river.
